notes:
Key contact: CTO Elena Marquez (very product-driven). Primary goal: replace brittle internal embed pipeline and reduce per-query cost for semantic search across product docs and support transcripts. Evaluating Hosted API first to validate quality, then Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost.

POC details and feedback: 
- Hosted embeddings used as baseline; ran 3 weighty tests: single-query embedding latency, bulk S3->embeds batch job, and hybrid vector search latency under concurrent loads.
- Wanted 1536-d embeddings (team used OpenAI ada-embedding-002 baseline previously) — trialing Redwood models at 1536 and 1024 dims.
- Throughput targets: 150-200 embedding req/s sustained during business hours; batch pipeline must ingest 2-5M documents monthly (peak jobs of ~250k/day).
- Search perf goals: P95 query latency <150ms for online search across 8M vectors; cost sensitivity suggests need for prefix/KV cache + intelligent batching for long-running multi-turn reranks.
- Integrations: primary vector DB candidates Pinecone (preferred by infra), Weaviate (interesting for on-prem), and an in-house Milvus cluster. Need guidance on connector patterns and consistency semantics for eventual Dedicated deployment.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, envelope encryption via KMS, and audit logs for all inference calls. Data residency: EU customers must be pinned to EU region.
- Quote reaction: "we need predictable token costs — hosted moved fast for validation but Dedicated must make the unit economics work." — CTO

Open items: detailed Dedicated sizing (GPU types & pool sizes), SLA language for mid-market, billing cadence for batch embed jobs, proof of concept showing cost-per-embed delta vs OpenAI for same throughput.
